items.prompt: The toy cost model adds a 1,000-point penalty tax whenever a packing is illegal (overlap or overflow).
items.explain: Both clips: illegality is taxed at +1,000. That term dominates the bad overflow seed (~1,044).

items.prompt: On the starter energy landscape, the bad overflow seed vs the golden legal packing sit near which costs?
items.explain: Bad seed ≈ 1,044 (mostly the +1,000 tax). Golden drops below the penalty floor to about 36 (deadspace + a small HPWL proxy).

items.prompt: In the execution loop, saSwap proposes a neighbor by…
choices: Exchanging two modules’ origin coordinates while keeping their sizes fixed
items.explain: The clip: saSwap exchanges module origin (lower-left) coordinates; dimensions stay fixed. Soft-module reshape is the next lab.

items.prompt: Under the Metropolis criterion at high temperature T, a worsening move (ΔC > 0) is accepted…
choices: Never — only improving moves are legal
Only after T has already reached T_min
items.explain: High T: P = e^(−ΔC / T) lets the search escape bad local seeds. Improving moves (ΔC ≤ 0) are accepted immediately.

items.prompt: The clip says annealing is only as good as its…
items.explain: Short clip: simple coordinate swapping is a starting point; pairing SA with B*-trees, sequence pairs, or soft-module edits unlocks real flexibility.

items.prompt: Which implementation trap is called quenching?
choices: Pairing annealing with a B*-tree so overlap is zero by construction
Rescoring cost immediately after every saSwap
Cooling T so fast that the search never escapes the initial bad seed
Accepting ΔC ≤ 0 moves at high temperature
items.explain: Both clips list three traps: no legality penalty, forgetting to rescore after a swap, and cooling too fast (quenching).
